subject: CPRA service provider scope, subprocessors, and US-only fallback plan
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Health Legal <privacy@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CPRA: service provider scope, subprocessors, and onshore fallback

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal at Acme Health has a few follow-ups before we can route a draft DPA to contracting. Specifically we need:

1) Confirmation that Redwood will act as a "service provider" under CPRA (i.e., not a "share" for sale) and a short mapping to the DPA/Privacy Addendum that shows the relevant clauses.
2) A current roster of subprocessors that may process Acme Health data, with country of processing and whether they have onshore-only options for US-resident data.
3) A proposed onshore-only fallback plan: if a service or subprocessor in a restricted country is unavailable, can Redwood fail over to US-only capacity and provide evidence of the change of control and routing? We need the high-level operational steps and estimated RTO/RPO.
4) Evidence artifacts: SOC 2 summary (latest), encryption-at-rest proof of concept (screenshots acceptable), and a network/dataflow diagram showing where telemetry and logs are stored.

Can you send an initial package by EOD Tuesday (2027-02-16)? If you prefer, we can accept an interim package and follow with the SOC 2 report once redacted.

Thanks — we aim to finish legal review quickly once we have these items.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_evidence_request_20270214.pdf (reference)

Team — forwarding Acme's ask. Timeline: they want an initial package by EOD Tue (48 hours). High priority — likely enterprise contract.

My proposed split:
- Ben: produce subprocessor roster + note which subprocessors support US-only routing and the operational steps to flip on US capacity (include estimated RTO/RPO). Also include the CSV of current ASNs/regions we use for traffic egress.
- Karthik: legal mapping to CPRA/CPRA additions; confirm language we can commit to (service provider vs. sale) and finalize a short DPA addendum draft. We should avoid broad transfer language; propose a fallback that routes to US-dedicated fleet.
- Evelyn: pull SOC 2 summary and encryption screenshots; prepare a sanitized dataflow diagram that doesn't include PII samples.

Notes for response to Acme: be explicit about which artifacts are interim vs. final (SOC 2 full report vs. summary), and call out that some telemetry exports are transient and stored on third-party infra with contractual constraints.

I'll consolidate and send to Acme Tue morning if we can hit the artifacts. If any blocker (legal or infra) by Monday EOD, call it out.

Thanks — Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Enterprise Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CPRA: service provider scope, subprocessors, and onshore fallback

Olga / team — quick status. I attached a working subprocessor_roster.csv (attachment stub) with columns: vendor, function, country, onshore_option (yes/no), notes. Highlights:
- Primary infra: public cloud providers (us-west/us-east regions) — these support US-only routing.
- Secondary telemetry vendor: TelemetryCo (eu-hosted by default) but they have a US-only region that requires a new contract amendment (estimated 2-3 weeks to onboard).
- VectorSearch vendor: Indexly (US customers only option available) — already enabled for some dedicated customers.

Onshore fallback plan (high-level):
1) Detect degraded subprocessor in restricted region (health checks + egress failures).
2) Fail traffic to configured US-region endpoints (DNS + load balancer switch) with a prefetched model variant in US pool.
3) Rehydrate KV cache/replicate essential telemetry to US NFS from edge caches (we keep 72h of rolling cache).
4) Notify customer via the Redwood Console and open incident in their workspace; provide explicit timestamped attestations of failover.
Estimated RTO: 4-8 minutes for routing + 30-90 minutes to fully rehydrate telemetry (depends on backlog). RPO: up to 15 minutes for requests that relied on ephemeral edge caches.

I'll clean the roster and export a CSV. Also attaching a short operational playbook stub for the failover steps (playbook stub).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: subprocessor_roster.csv, failover_playbook.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 14:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CPRA: service provider scope, subprocessors, and onshore fallback

Thanks Ben — this is very helpful. A few legal/contract notes before we send: 

1) Service provider language: we can commit to CPRA service provider treatment for the processing categories Acme described (model inference, telemetry related to API usage). I'll draft a short clause for the addendum that explicitly states: "Redwood acts as a service provider under CPRA and will not sell Covered Data." Keep it scoped to data types in the SOW.
2) Fallback commitments: Legal is comfortable with operational fallback descriptions and an incident attestation, but we should avoid SLA-like guarantees for RTO/RPO in the DPA addendum. Instead propose target windows in the playbook and include a paragraph that Redwood will use reasonable commercial efforts to route to US-only capacity.
3) Subprocessor evidence: we can provide a roster and redacted contractual attestations (country, role, encryption claims). For SOC 2, provide a redacted report and a SOC 2 summary PDF. For encryption-at-rest proof, screenshots of key-management console (no secret values) are fine.

I'll produce a one-page DPA addendum draft and a mapping table showing CPRA clauses -> Redwood DPA locations. Expect a first pass by EOD Mon.

-Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find our initial package attached and summarized below. This is intended to get your legal team comfortable while we finalize a short DPA addendum.

What we enclosed (interim package):
- subprocessor_roster.csv (redacted): vendor, processing function, country, onshore_option flag. Note: TelemetryCo is EU-hosted by default but offers US-region hosting requiring contract amendment.
- redwood_soc2_summary.pdf: executive summary of our latest SOC 2 with scope notes and a link to a redacted report in our secure drive.
- dpa_addendum_draft.docx: one-page CPRA-focused addendum that: (i) confirms Redwood acts as a service provider for the listed processing categories, (ii) limits "sale" language, and (iii) includes a fallback commitment paragraph using "reasonable commercial efforts" language rather than hard SLA windows.
- failover_playbook.pdf (operational stub): shows detection, DNS/loadbalancer failover, model rehydration, and incident attestation steps. RTO/RPO targets are listed as operational targets (not contractual commitments): RTO target 4-8 minutes for routing; full telemetry rehydration 30-90 minutes; RPO up to 15 minutes in edge-cache scenarios.
- encryption_screenshots.zip (screenshots only): key-management console views showing KMS usage with audit timestamps.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether a redacted SOC 2 report is sufficient or if Acme requires the full report under NDA.
2) If TelemetryCo US-region is required, we can amend our contract with them; expect a 2-3 week timeline for activation and a separate change notice.
3) If you want specific RTO/RPO in the DPA, we can discuss a separate operational SLA add-on with limited scope (e.g., dedicated fleet).

We can hop on a short call to walk through the plan — available Tue 2pm PT / Wed 10am PT.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Enterprise Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
